    Small PlatesOffice party beef and onion sausage rollsOn the company card, before Carol's flight gets cancelled.How to make it2 onions, sliced20g butter300g beef mince200g pork mince1 tsp dried thyme40g breadcrumbs2 eggs (1 for the filling, 1 beaten for glazing)2 sheets of puff pastry1 tbsp sesame seeds200g tomato relishFry the onions in the butter until golden, then cool.Mix the minces with the onions, thyme, breadcrumbs, one egg and salt.Cut the pastry in half, lay a log of filling along each strip, roll and seal.Brush with egg, sprinkle with sesame and cut into pieces.Bake at 200°C until golden. Serve with relish.Mary's cheeseboard camembert, baked with honeyHot camembert with rosemary and honey, toast, grapes and fig jamHow to make it250g camembert1 garlic clove, in slivers1 sprig rosemary, in small sprigs1 tbsp honey1 baguette, sliced2 tbsp olive oil300g grapes4 tbsp fig jamSit the camembert in a small dish and cut slits in the top. Push in garlic and rosemary and drizzle with honey.Bake at 180°C until soft in the middle.Brush the baguette slices with oil and toast.Serve the cheese hot on a board with toasts, grapes and fig jam.SupperZenotek smash cheeseburger slidersClay's pitch to win over Walter Davis and Data City.How to make it2 onions, sliced20g butter4 tbsp mayonnaise2 tbsp tomato sauce1 tsp American mustard1 tbsp chopped dill pickles, plus slices to serve600g beef mince6 slices of cheddar, halved12 brioche slider buns1 tbsp vegetable oilSlowly fry the onions in the butter until jammy.Mix the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, mustard and chopped pickles into a sauce.Roll the mince into balls, smash flat in a very hot pan with the vegetable oil, season and cook, then flip and top each with half a slice of cheddar.Toast the buns and fill with sauce, patty, onions and pickles.Mary from HR's approved roast salmonMary from HR has signed off on it, and it is strictly non-denominationalHow to make it800g side of salmon, skin on2 tbsp wholegrain mustard1 tbsp honey1 lemon1 bunch dill800g small potatoes2 tbsp olive oil300g green beans20g butterBoil the potatoes for 18 minutes, drain and crush with the oil and salt.Mix the mustard, honey, lemon zest and half the chopped dill.Lay the salmon on a lined tray, spread with the glaze and roast at 200°C for 15 minutes.Boil the beans for 4 minutes and toss with the butter.Scatter the salmon with the rest of the dill and serve with lemon wedges, potatoes and beans.After the ShowRed and green cupcakesVanilla cupcakes with red and green buttercream. Mary says no Cronuts.How to make it275g butter, soft150g caster sugar2 eggs200g self-raising flour120ml full cream milk300g icing sugar1 pack food colouring (red and green)Beat some of the butter with the sugar, add the eggs, then fold in the flour and milk.Divide into cupcake cases and bake at 180°C.Cool completely.Beat the remaining butter with the icing sugar, tint half red and half green.Pipe on top of the cupcakes.Coolers and FloatsCinnamon vanilla eggnogHomemade egg custard nog with cinnamon and nutmegHow to make it4 eggs (yolks only)100g caster sugar600ml full cream milk200ml thickened cream1 cinnamon stick2 tsp vanilla extract1 whole nutmegWhisk the yolks with the sugar.Heat the milk, cream, cinnamon and vanilla until steaming, then slowly whisk into the yolks.Return to the pan and stir over low heat until it coats a spoon.Strain and chill.Pour into glasses and grate fresh nutmeg over the top.
